attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Need a direct-sum or shared-computation lower bound converting any small selector/promise-solver circuit into a subthreshold cycle-24 cover. No such theorem is available, and it is plausibly false for structured selectors.
steps: Start with the cycle-24 condition that positive fibers and negative product fibers have no subthreshold nonuniform hitting cover.
Try to conclude C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon} by arguing every H_N circuit induces such a cover.
Observe that a circuit can first compute a shared selector Sel_N(x) and query only G_N(x,Sel_N(x)).
The induced cover over decoded selector values may have large additive cost because shared gates are replicated when charged per fiber.
Therefore additive hitting-cover hardness does not exclude selector-plus-promise-solver circuits.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The work supplies a valid new obstruction for the carrier lower bound, but it does not prove any lower bound for H_N and does not establish SAT notin P/poly.

assumptions: Sel_N:{0,1}^N->[M] is a total circuit of size s_N.
For all x with H_N(x)=1, SAT(G_N(x,Sel_N(x)))=1.
For all x with H_N(x)=0, every generated query is unsatisfiable, so the selected query is negative.
P_N agrees with SAT on V_S={G_N(x,Sel_N(x)):x in {0,1}^N}.
The generator and selector outputs are encoded with O(log M) overhead and no extra nonuniform advice beyond the named circuits.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{1<=j<=M} SAT(G_N(x,j)) on |x|=N, with M=N^q, query length L=(log N)^d, and generator circuit size C(G_N)<=N^{rho+o(1)}.

target object: SAT on L-bit formula encodings against nonuniform circuits of size L^c for every fixed c, yielding the route consequence SAT notin P/poly if the source lower bound is valid and target transfer is clean.
controlled interface: target circuits enter only by replacing each SAT(G_N(x,j)) call; the source audit allows arbitrary nonuniform promise solvers on actual generated ranges as potential leakage.

target-preserving condition: q<1+epsilon, rho<1+epsilon, L is polylogarithmic with lookup not subthreshold, and no selected-image advice or promise solver computes the carrier below N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.

equations.label: selector_upper_bound
equations.valid_when: Valid when Sel_N is a genuine positive selector and P_N is correct on the complete selected image V_S.

equations.label: source_obstruction
equations.valid_when: Applies after generator overhead is below threshold and the asserted lower bound is in the same nonuniform circuit model.

equations.label: target_transfer_unchanged

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Route-gate sharpening: converts cycle-24 hitting-cover hardness into a stronger shared-selector leakage falsifier for the source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a generated-OR carrier H_N, any small valid selector for a satisfying generated query, together with a small promise solver on the selected image, gives a direct circuit upper bound for H_N. Hence an N^{1+epsilon} source lower bound must rule out all subthreshold selector-plus-selected-range-solver pairs, not only additive hitting covers.

assumptions: Sel_N is valid in the sense of the selector_range_falsifier lemma.
Formula encodings have length L=(log N)^d.
Nonuniform circuits may hardwire the finite selected image and its SAT labels.
definitions: Let sigma(Sel) be the exponent with |V_S|=N^{sigma(Sel)+o(1)}.
The lookup solver stores the SAT label of each formula in V_S and tests equality against the L-bit input.
The corollary is a source-model upper bound, not a proof of SAT easiness outside V_S.

equations.valid_when: Valid when P_N only needs promise correctness on V_S and equality tests on L-bit encodings are allowed.

candidate_lemmas.statement: If a valid selector has small selected image, then equality-DNF lookup gives the needed promise solver, so selected-image entropy is a necessary source-plausibility condition.

assumptions: Cycle-24 cover measure is additive over blocks or fibers.
The selector circuit can reuse internal gates before its output is decoded into j.
No direct-sum lower bound for the decoded fibers has been proved.
definitions: A positive-fiber cover charges separate circuits for pieces inside each P_j={x:SAT(G_N(x,j))=1}.
A selector computes one index-valued map and then tests only the selected query.
Shared selector cost is not comparable to the sum over all fiber cover costs without an additional direct-sum theorem.

equations.label: cover_vs_selector_gap
equations.valid_when: Valid when circuit size counts shared gates once and decoding many output fibers can duplicate the same computation.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A carrier may pass all additive cover thresholds yet fail by one shared selector and one selected-range promise solver.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents overclaiming: cycle-24 cover gates are necessary but not sufficient for the generated-OR source lower bound.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Additive hitting-cover hardness does not by itself imply selector-range hardness, because a selector shares one computation across all fibers instead of paying the sum of separate positive-fiber covers.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 25 adds a shared-selector leakage gate. A generated-OR carrier can be easy via one compact selector and a promise SAT solver on only the selected image, even when additive semantic or hitting covers look expensive. Thus the valid source obligation is not merely high range entropy or label balance; it is lower bounding every selector-plus-selected-range-solver pair above N^{1+epsilon-o(1)} while preserving q,rho<1+epsilon for the target bridge.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The route lemma is proved under its typed assumptions. The remaining gap for any P-vs-NP route is unjustified existence of such a low explicit positive certificate; PRF-based natural-proof barriers make that existence implausible for standard target classes.
steps: Fix m and N=2^m; let H=TT(SAT_m).
Assume P_N is total, poly(N)-constructive, P_N(H)=1, and P_N(C)=0 for every truth table C computed by an m-input circuit of size m^k.
Let alpha_N be an explicit 1-certificate for P_N at H, so H extends alpha_N and every y extending alpha_N satisfies P_N(y)=1.
Define R_N to be the cylinder of all y extending alpha_N.
R_N is decidable in time poly(N) by checking the c(N) constrained coordinates; no query to P_N is required.
The uniform measure of R_N is exactly 2^{-c(N)}; for c(N)<=a log_2 N this is at least N^{-a}.
If a target circuit truth table y belonged to R_N, then y extends alpha_N, hence P_N(y)=1, contradicting the separator soundness P_N(y)=0.
Therefore R_N is constructive, large at the stated threshold, and useful against SIZE(m^k).
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This only certifies that one family of proof objects naturalizes. It neither constructs a separator P_N nor proves SAT lacks polynomial-size circuits, and it is consistent with the falsifier that all valid separators have superlogarithmic or nonconstructive positive certificates.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-aware lower-bound route: positive-certificate naturalization gate

assumptions: P_N is a total predicate on all N-bit truth tables, not merely a promise verifier on SAT and circuits.
alpha_N is a partial assignment to c(N) coordinates and is a 1-certificate: every y extending alpha_N satisfies P_N(y)=1.
The target class is fixed as SIZE(m^k), or another named circuit class closed under truth-table encoding.
The certificate coordinates and required SAT bits are obtainable in poly(N); brute-force SAT on m-bit formulas is allowed because 2^m=N.
Usefulness means R_N contains no truth table computed by the target circuit class.
definitions: source object: a total poly(N)-time decidable truth-table predicate P_N:{0,1}^N->{0,1} together with an explicit positive certificate alpha_N for TT(SAT_m).
target object: a Razborov-Rudich style natural property R_N useful against Boolean circuits on m inputs of size m^k, with N=2^m.
controlled interface: extract the cylinder of all truth tables agreeing with alpha_N and use the 1-certificate promise to place the cylinder inside P_N.
target-preserving condition: alpha_N is computable or listable in poly(N), TT(SAT_m) satisfies alpha_N, alpha_N forces P_N=1 on the whole cylinder, and P_N rejects every target circuit truth table.

equations.label: truth_table_scale
equations.valid_when: Valid when truth tables are indexed by all m-bit inputs and the certificate constrains coordinates of that table.

equations.label: extracted_property
equations.valid_when: Applies when alpha_N is a partial assignment and membership is tested by checking its constrained coordinates.

equations.label: density_threshold
equations.valid_when: Valid when the constrained coordinates are distinct and the ambient distribution is uniform over all N-bit truth tables.

equations.label: usefulness_transfer

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: The lemma fails if alpha_N is not a genuine 1-certificate, is nonconstructive beyond poly(N), has c(N)=omega(log N) for the desired density, or P_N is only a promise object without a total extension.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Barrier audit bridge: it converts low positive certificate complexity at SAT into a natural property and therefore quarantines witnessed-acceptance separator routes under standard PRF-based natural-proof obstructions.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Let N=2^m. If a poly(N)-constructive separator P_N over truth tables accepts TT(SAT_m), rejects every m-input circuit of size m^k, and has an explicit 1-certificate alpha_N for TT(SAT_m) of size c(N), then the alpha_N-cylinder is a natural property of density 2^{-c(N)} useful against SIZE(m^k). In particular c(N)<=a log_2 N is a valid natural-proof object, not a barrier escape.

assumptions: The DNF list is explicit or uniform enough to scan in poly(N).
Each term has only equality literals y_i=b, with repeated coordinates removed.
The separator rejects all target circuit truth tables, not merely typical or random circuits.
definitions: DNF separator means a total truth-table predicate whose accepting certificates are listed terms over truth-table coordinates.
The SAT-satisfied term is found by evaluating each term on TT(SAT_m), using poly(N) time for coordinate SAT decisions.
The term cylinder is contained in P_N because the top gate is OR.
The quantitative threshold is w(N)<=a log_2 N for density at least N^{-a}.

equations.label: dnf_density
equations.valid_when: Valid when the DNF has an accepting term on SAT and every term has width at most w(N).

equations.label: dnf_natural_threshold
equations.valid_when: Applies in the polynomial-density regime required by the natural-proof largeness condition.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A CNF, threshold circuit, or implicit search proof need not expose a low-width accepting term, so this corollary cannot be invoked without a positive certificate.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Concrete corollary for DNF-shaped proof objects; witnessed acceptance is enough to create largeness.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If an explicit DNF separator P_N=OR_{j<=M} T_j has M=poly(N), every term width at most w(N), P_N(TT(SAT_m))=1, and P_N rejects SIZE(m^k), then some SAT-satisfied term gives a natural property of density at least 2^{-w(N)} useful against SIZE(m^k). Thus w=O(log N) DNF separator routes naturalize.

assumptions: The proof object may be syntactically low width but acceptance need not be witnessed by a small term.
No distributional lower bound on P_N^{-1}(1) is supplied independently.
definitions: Positive certificate complexity C_1(P_N,TT(SAT_m)) controls density of a SAT-containing cylinder.
Negative certificate complexity on rejected circuit truth tables controls only local exclusion and gives no lower bound on acceptance density.
A width-1 CNF fixing all bits of a designated truth table can have density 2^{-N}, showing that clause width alone is not a largeness certificate.
This is a falsifier for symmetric claims that any low-width Boolean description of a separator is automatically natural.

equations.label: cnf_singleton_density
equations.valid_when: Valid when the CNF consists of N unit clauses fixing a single N-bit truth table.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the CNF additionally implies a small accepting subcube containing SAT, then the first lemma, not this asymmetry, applies.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Prevents overextension of the positive-certificate lemma to CNF or rejection-certificate routes.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Low negative certificate complexity or low CNF width is not enough to naturalize a separator. The naturalization uses a large accepting cylinder containing SAT, whereas small rejecting cylinders around target circuits may leave only an exponentially tiny accepting set.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if the proposed lower-bound method has no explicit total predicate P_N or if its SAT acceptance is not witnessed by a small positive certificate.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote only if the method proves superlogarithmic positive certificate complexity, nonconstructive but target-preserving structure, or another certified non-natural feature while retaining usefulness against the target class.

Low CNF width or low negative certificate complexity does not imply largeness; singleton CNFs show threshold collapse.

DNF witnessed-acceptance routes with O(log N) term width therefore naturalize; low-width CNF or negative-certificate routes are a concrete falsifier to the symmetric claim. This is route-level barrier progress, not evidence for P != NP.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is conditional. It does not construct a cap-compatible uniform source with constant epsilon, linear certificate rate c, and a kappa-dense locatable set of lengths containing at least one hard accepted witness.
steps: Define L_V on length n_m=(1+c)m by parsing the first c m bits as y and the last m bits as x; output zero if A_V(m,y)=0 and otherwise output the emitted bit T_{m,y}(x).
Uniformity: because Eval_V(m,y,x) runs in 2^{O(m)} and n_m is linear in m, L_V is decidable in 2^{O(n_m)}, hence is an E target object.
Lower-bound transfer: if a size-S circuit computes L_V at length n_m, fix y=y* for an accepted hard witness; the restricted circuit computes T_{m,y*} with size S+O(m).
Therefore S>2^{epsilon m-o(m)}, giving exponent epsilon/(1+c) on the multiplexed lengths.

If source lengths are uniformly kappa-dense, define the all-length padded language by ignoring extra pad bits and using the located predecessor source length; this loses the usual factor kappa, so every delta<epsilon/((1+c)kappa) is valid.
Cap audit: if the verifier has fixed-slice checkpoint profile alpha_V, then any claim epsilon>alpha_V is internally inconsistent before transfer.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a route-level bridge from a strong MCSP-carrier source to E lower bounds. It does not prove P != NP and does not even supply the required hard MCSP carrier source.

assumptions: For each relevant m there exists an accepted y* with C(T_{m,y*})>2^{epsilon m}. Universal hardness of all accepted y is not required.
Rejected certificates are mapped to the zero slice, so only accepted hard witnesses transfer.
The source length set M has a uniform predecessor/locator usable in E for padding to all target lengths.

Barrier audit: the carrier image has size at most 2^{cm+O(1)} among 2^{2^m} tables, so it is non-large; any dense constructive repair would become a natural-proofs falsifier under standard pseudorandom-function assumptions.
definitions: source object: a uniform MCSP-carrier verifier/emitter V_m with certificate y of length at most c m, acceptance bit A_V(m,y), and emitted truth table T_{m,y}:{0,1}^m -> {0,1}.
target object: an E-uniform Boolean language L_V whose length (1+c)m slice is the certificate-index multiplexer (y,x) -> A_V(m,y)T_{m,y}(x).
controlled interface: hardwire an accepted certificate y* in any circuit for the multiplexer to obtain a circuit of essentially the same size for the hard MCSP no-side slice.
target-preserving condition: the source lengths are uniformly locatable and kappa-dense, Eval_V runs in 2^{O(m)}, c,kappa,epsilon are constants, and no advice or nonuniform selector is used.

candidate_lemmas.statement: Rate-costed certificate-index multiplexer bridge: existential hard accepted MCSP-carrier witnesses suffice without a selector, at exact exponent loss 1+c. If a uniform verifier/emitter V at source length m has certificates y of length at most c m and some accepted y* emits a table T_{m,y*} with circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m}, then the target multiplexer L_V(y,x)=A_V(m,y)T_{m,y}(x) on n=(1+c)m input bits has circuit complexity greater than 2^{epsilon m-o(m)}. If such m are uniformly kappa-dense, padding gives every delta<epsilon/((1+c)kappa).

assumptions: At least one accepted y is hard at threshold 2^{epsilon m}.
The target circuit class is closed under fixing input bits to constants.
The verifier acceptance bit is incorporated in the multiplexed function definition.
definitions: C(F) denotes Boolean circuit size for the full length-n truth table.
Accepted slices are those with A_V(m,y)=1; rejected slices are forced to zero in L_V.
Same-length extraction means trying to output one canonical T_{m,y} without carrying y as an input.

equations.label: hardest_slice_dominates

candidate_lemmas.statement: Easy accepted certificates contaminate same-length extraction but are not a falsifier for the multiplexed target. The multiplexer lower bound is controlled by the hardest accepted slice, not by the easiest accepted slice.

assumptions: The source threshold is C(T_{m,y*})>2^{epsilon m} for constant epsilon>0.
The only transfer mechanism is hardwiring the certificate-index bits in the multiplexer.

n_m=m+r(m)+O(log m) is the multiplexed target length.
delta_m is the induced target exponent before any kappa-density padding.

candidate_lemmas.statement: If certificate length r(m) is superlinear, certificate-index multiplexing no longer yields a constant-exponent E lower bound from a 2^{epsilon m} source threshold. Linear certificates are not cosmetic; they are quantitatively necessary for this route.
